THIS MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS APPEAL HAVING BEEN FINALLY HEARD ON 08.01.2025, THE COURT ON THE SAME DAY DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 MACA NO. 341 OF 2018  3  JUDGMENT Dated this the 08th day of January, 2025
The petitioner in O.P.(M.V.) No.929/2011 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Thalassery is the appellant herein.
The respondents in the O.P. are the respondents herein.

The petitioner filed the above O.P. under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, claiming compensation for the injuries sustained in a motor vehicle accident that occurred on 07.02.2011.
2.

According to the petitioner, on 07.02.2011 at about 04.30 p.m., while he was standing near to the bus waiting shelter at Pandialamukku, a car bearing Registration No.KL-58B/9643 driven by the 2nd respondent in a rash and negligent manner hit him down.
As a result of which, he sustained serious injuries.
The 1st respondent is the owner, the 2nd respondent is the driver and 3rd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
According to the him, the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, he filed the OP claiming a compensation of Rs.25,00,000/-.
3. The 1st and 2nd respondents remained ex-parte.
The 3rd respondent/insurer filed a written statement, admitting the policy and disputing the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It was further contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner.
The evidence in the case consists of the oral testimony of PW1 & PW2 and documentary evidence Exts.A1 to A12 and C1.
No evidence was adduced by the respondents.

sentences.text: After evaluating the evidence on record, the Tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.15,62,500/-.
6. Aggrieved by the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal, the petitioner preferred this appeal.

7. Now the point that arises for consideration is the following:
Whether the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

8. Heard Sri.C.P.Peethambaran, the learned Counsel appearing for the appellant, and Sri.Sebastian Varghese, the learned Standing Counsel for the 3rd respondent.
9.
The Point: In this case the accident and valid policy of the offending vehicle are admitted.
Though in the written statement the 3 rd respondent has contended that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the petitioner, at the time of arguments such a contention was not taken.
The petitioner has produced Ext.A1, copy of the FIR involved in the crime registered against the driver of the offending vehicle, in respect to the above accident.
Therefore, the 3rd respondent, being the insurer, is liable to MACA NO. 341 OF 2018 2025:KER:1127 indemnify the compensation, which is liable to be awarded against the owner of the offending vehicle.
10. The petitioner was aged 60 years on the date of the accident, on .07.02.2011.
According to the petitioner, he was working as a watchman, earning Rs.4,500/- per month.
The Tribunal also fixed his income at Rs.4,500/-.

As per the dictum laid down in the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ramachandrappa v. Manger, Royal Sundaram Alliance Insurance Co. Ltd. [2011 (13) SCC 236],
the notional income of a cooli during the year 2011 is libale to be fixed at Rs.8,000/-.

sentences.text: Therefore, in the light of the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Minu Rout and Others v. Satya Pradyumna Mohapatra and Others, (2013) 10 SCC 695, the notional income of the petitioner is fixed at Rs.8,000/-.

sentences.text:
11. Since the petitioner sustained very serious injuries in the accident that occurred on 07.02.2011,
the Tribunal fixed his functional disability at 100%.
During the pendency of the appeal, he died on 23.05.2021.
That means, he was bed ridden for a period of 10 years and 3 1/2 months, before he died.

Therefore, towards 'expenses for nursing care', he is eligible for the expense of a bystander @
Rs.5,000/- per month for 10 years and 3 1/2 months i.e., Rs.5,000x123.5.
Therefore, compensation MACA NO. 341 OF 2018 2025:KER:1127 towards expenses for nursing care will come to Rs.6,17,500/-.

Since a sum of Rs.6,17,500/- is awarded on the head expenses for nursing care,
Rs.41,200/- awarded on the head bystander expenses is to be deducted.

12. Since, on the date of accident, he was aged 60 years, the multiplier to be applied is 9, as held in the decision in National Insurance Co.Ltd v Pranay Sethi [(2017) 16 SCC 680].

sentences.text: In the above circumstances, compensation towards loss of disability will come to Rs.8,64,000/-.
Towards the head 'pain and sufferings', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.2,00,000/-, which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.
The petitioner was bed ridden for a period of 10 years and 3 1/2 months, till he breathed his last.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards pain and suffering is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.5,00,000/-.
15.

Towards the head compensation for 'loss of amenities', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.1,00,000/-,
which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.
After the accident the petitioner was bed ridden for a period of a 10 years and 31/2 months, till he breathed his last.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded MACA NO. 341 OF 2018 2025:KER:1127 towards 'loss of amenities' is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.2,00,000/-.
16.

Towards the head compensation for 'extra nourishment', the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/-,
which according to the learned counsel for the petitioner, is on the lower side.
The petitioner was bed ridden for a period of a 10 years and 3 1/2 months.

In the above circumstances, I hold that the compensation awarded towards extra nourishment is on the lesser side, and hence, it is enhanced to Rs.50,000/-.
17.
Since the disability of the petitioner is 100%, further compensation on the head loss of earning is not required.
Therefore, Rs.27000/- awarded on the head loss of earning is deducted.
No change is required, in the amounts awarded on other heads, as the compensation awarded on those heads appears to be just and reasonable.
18. Therefore, the petitioner/ appellant is entitled to get a total compensation of Rs.28,35,800/-, as modified and recalculated above and given in the table below, for easy reference.

In the result, this Appeal is allowed in part, and the 3rd respondent is directed to deposit a total compensation of Rs.28,35,800/- (Rupees Twenty Eight Lakhs Thirty Five Thousand Eight Hundred Only), less the amount already deposited, if any, along with interest @ 9% per annum, (enhanced compensation will carry only 8% interest) from the date of the petition till realisation, excluding interest for a period of 109 days, the MACA NO. 341 OF 2018 2025:KER:1127 period of delay in filing the appeal, with proportionate costs, within a period of two months from today.
20 . On depositing the aforesaid amount, the Tribunal shall disburse the entire amount to the petitioner, excluding court fee payable, if any, without delay, as per rules.
